headline.purpose: Uppercase section titles, always paired with the accent underline.

title.purpose: Card-level headings — experience role, skill category.

body.purpose: Prose copy, mission bullets, form labels; opacity steps down emphasis rather than color.

label.purpose: Live/technical content in JetBrains Mono — badges, timestamps, chapter numbers, terminal chrome.

shadows.name: ambient-rest
shadows.purpose: Default barely-there separation for glass panels at rest.

shadows.name: interactive-hover
shadows.purpose: Accent-tinted lift on card/tab hover, paired with the cursor-tracked glow and a border shift to accent/50.

motion.name: reveal-ease
motion.purpose: Signature scroll-reveal curve: 24px rise, ~0.6s, once per viewport. Used for nearly every scroll-triggered entrance.

motion.name: float
motion.purpose: Gentle vertical bob for the hero's floating tech-stack badges.

components.name: Glass Card
components.description: The system's core surface: translucent, blurred, hairline-bordered. Live implementation adds a cursor-tracked radial glow on hover (see DESIGN.md Elevation & Depth); this static snippet approximates the hover state.
components.html:
Ingénieur Logiciel — Backend NodeJS

Design and development of custom applications aligned with the overall architecture.
components.css: .ds-card { position:relative; overflow:hidden; border-radius:16px; border:1px solid rgba(234,242,250,0.1); background:rgba(10,14,20,0.5); backdrop-filter: blur(24px); padding:24px; box-shadow: 0 10px 25px -5px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); transition: transform 0.3s, border-color 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: rgba(61,169,252,0.5); box-shadow: 0 20px 40px -10px rgba(61,169,252,0.10); } .ds-card-glow { position:absolute; inset:0; opacity:0; transition:opacity 0.3s; background: radial-gradient(220px circle at 50% 0%, rgba(61,169,252,0.12), transparent 65%); pointer-events:none; } .ds-card:hover .ds-card-glow { opacity:1; } .ds-card-content { position:relative; } .ds-card-title { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight:700; font-size:16px; margin:0 0 8px; color:#EAF2FA; } .ds-card-body { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size:14px; line-height:1.6; color: rgba(234,242,250,0.7); margin:0; }

narrative.overview:
This portfolio reads like a live infrastructure dashboard, not a résumé with a coat of paint. A network-topology particle field drifts behind every section; a terminal-styled window frames the hero photo, complete with traffic-light dots and a `~/t — zsh` label; a live clock ticks in the navbar; a status dot pulses "available." The visitor isn't reading about an engineer — they're looking at a console the engineer built and left running.

The personality is precise and quietly confident: technical credibility is shown through the fidelity of small details (a correctly-drawn radial gauge, a timeline spine that fills as you scroll, a cursor-tracked glass glow) rather than through loud claims or decoration. Nothing here is playful or cartoonish, and nothing is generic corporate-stock-photo either — the confidence comes from restraint and precision, not volume.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first glass morphism: translucent, blurred panels floating over a near-black canvas, never opaque flat cards.
A single narrow accent pairing (Signal Blue + Uptime Green) used sparingly against a desaturated dark neutral field.
JetBrains Mono marks anything "live" or technical — timestamps, badges, chapter numbers, terminal chrome — as a deliberate second voice alongside Inter's prose.
Motion is diagnostic, not decorative: progress rings draw, timeline spines fill, elements reveal on scroll — always reading as data becoming visible, never as flourish.

rules.name: The Restrained Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue at full strength is reserved for interactive or active elements. Everywhere else it drops to 5–15% opacity for glows and dividers.

rules.name: The Mono Signal Rule
rules.body: Anything that represents live, technical, or numeric state renders in JetBrains Mono. Anything that represents written thought renders in Inter.

rules.name: The Glass Surface Rule
rules.body: Every elevated surface is translucent + blurred + hairline-bordered — never an opaque fill.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: If it's clickable or a status marker, it's fully round. If it's a content container, it's 2xl. Nothing in between.

dos: Do render every elevated surface as glass: translucent Void Black, backdrop-blur, hairline base-content/10 border.
Do keep interactive/status elements fully pill-shaped and containers at 2xl radius, never mixed.
Do render technical/live content — timestamps, counters, badges, chapter numbers — in JetBrains Mono.
Do reserve full-strength Signal Blue for interactive/active state; use low-opacity tints for ambient glow and dividers.
Do animate reveals with the site's signature ease ([0.22, 1, 0.36, 1], ~24px rise, once per viewport) so motion feels like one consistent system, not per-component defaults.
Do maintain the devopslight counterpart in parity whenever a new color or component ships — same role, deeper/lighter tone swap, never a hardcoded dark-only value.
donts: Don't use opaque, flat card backgrounds — the glass treatment is load-bearing identity, not a stylistic option per component.
Don't introduce saturated colors outside Signal Blue / Uptime Green plus the semantic amber/red pair; the palette is intentionally two-accent.
Don't repeat the terminal-chrome (traffic-light dots) motif elsewhere — it's a single deliberate accent, not a reusable component pattern.
Don't give inputs the same cursor-glow treatment as cards; that interaction is GlassCard's signature, not a generic hover effect to apply everywhere.
